Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a small right hemithorax with diminished vascular markings and an absent right hilar shadow (indicated by arrows), which are classic radiological signs of proximal absence of the right pulmonary artery. The other options typically present with hyperlucency (Swyer-James, congenital lobar emphysema), consolidation (pneumonia), or different anatomical anomalies not seen here.
